curriculumFinding: The Dutch full-time 2026–2027 bachelor has no formal graduation specialisations: 60 EC in each of Years 1–2, then two compulsory 6 EC courses, an 18 EC project and 30 EC open study. The adopted OER Article11.3 controls year allocation; the recruitment page mixes differently named chemistry units and places the modern-developments project differently. No duplicate old/new course versions are stacked. Zero-credit laboratory safety, Dutch diagnostic/remedial language study and mentorship/tutorials are recorded separately. BSA normally requires42first-yearEC. The basic pharmacochemistry practical precedes bioanalysis, molecular pharmacology, toxicology, molecular modelling and synthesis practicals. Project entry requires all first-year courses, all listed practicals including modelling, and120EC including open study for periods5–6. The exceptional periods2–3 project requires every other curricular course passed by31August. Project allocation considers preferences, motivation and capacity; apply by the published early-January deadline and register for XB_0140, Canvas and Onstage. Individual laboratory journal, thesis, talk and poster are required. Academic/professional attitude, practical execution, report and oral presentation each contribute25%; each must reach5.5. Open choices require prior board approval except stated university/listed-minor exemptions, at least12ECat300 and at most6ECat100; an overseas package can include one6ECmaster course that cannot be reused for a subsequent master. Attendance conditions follow individual manuals; honours and historic transition units are not additional requirements.
comparabilityFinding: The strongest attempted UCR programme has real contributions in pharmacology, molecular-cell biology, biochemistry and biomedical laboratory methods. Pharmacology explicitly teaches targets, drug–macromolecule interactions and quantitative pharmacokinetic models; these contributions are retained in the evidence. However, the completed composition is organised predominantly around disease biology, general neuroscience and general data/research methods. It does not implement the target’s defining progression from chemical structure/reactivity through synthesis, compound identification, bioanalysis/toxicology practicals and pharmaceutical molecular/computational modelling to experimental drug discovery. Generic machine learning, neural networks, anatomy, immunity and evidence synthesis cannot supply those missing chemical mechanisms and experimental design skills. Adding available recycling/inorganic chemistry or ecology does not establish medicinal/organic chemistry. A coherent biomedical programme is therefore not by itself a substantive pharmaceutical-sciences response. No defensible complete UCR alternative is established; this is not based on a matching-course quota, professional licensing or absence of a degree title.

alternatives.label: Molecular disease, pharmacology & biomedical research
alternatives.concept: The strongest defensible UCR response studies molecular and cellular disease, physiology, biochemistry, pharmacology, immunity, pathology, laboratory methods and quantitative evidence. It can address how drugs act on biological targets and how effectiveness and toxicity are evaluated, but it is a biomedical related-fields programme rather than pharmaceutical chemistry or drug-synthesis training.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by molecular disease mechanisms, pharmacology, biomedical laboratory work and quantitative research. The label states those supported emphases and avoids presenting the programme as Pharmaceutical Sciences or medicinal chemistry.
progression: Life-science, brain-and-behaviour, programming, mathematics, statistics and data foundations precede physiology, biochemistry, molecular-cell biology, laboratory work, anatomy and advanced pharmacology, pathology, immunity, neuroscience and evidence synthesis. HCBGATE101 and HCBGATE102 precede every dependent biomedical or psychology course, DISGATE102 precedes advanced quantitative work, and all exact planned terms pass. Eight courses are at 300 level.

core: Molecular and cellular disease, physiology and biological drug targets
Pharmacology, drug kinetics, therapeutic effects and toxicity
Medicinal and organic chemistry, molecular synthesis and compound optimisation
Biochemical, molecular and structural laboratory research
Mathematical, statistical, modelling and computational methods
Independent pharmaceutical research and responsible science
adjacent: Chemistry-focused pharmaceutical science and drug synthesis

What goes wrong inside cells during disease?

candidates.label: Medicinal chemistry, synthesis & compound optimisation
candidates.assessment: UCR has biochemistry but no cumulative organic or medicinal chemistry, synthesis practicals, compound identification, structure–activity optimisation, molecular modelling for pharmacochemists or computational pharmacochemistry. A second programme would therefore misrepresent general life science and data courses as a drug-discovery chemistry curriculum.

selection.assessment: One complete related-fields programme is defensible around molecular disease, pharmacology and biomedical research. It also covers the eligible biology-focused pharmaceutical direction. The remaining generator-backed chemistry-and-synthesis direction is defining but infeasible at UCR; because Alternative 2 fails, the sequential rule requires production to stop at one.
